candidates.title: Map resume facts into application fields

demandEvidence.chore: The post describes repeated manual entry of resume data into forms tailored to one or two companies.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I spent two hours every day filling my resume data to freshly developed forms made specifically to the hiring process of one or two companies.

ease.reason: A beginner can map supplied resume facts to sample fields; company-specific formats remain unknown.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: a narrow setup service might interest this group, but the discussion shows no purchase intent or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week manual-input mock can prepare values; company-specific forms and accuracy need human checks.

autonomy.reason: The proposed loop prepares a draft; a person must verify the inputs and complete the external action.

evidence.reason: The post states a daily two-hour resume-data entry task for company-specific forms, but gives no fields or examples.

experimentPlan.output: Prepare a reviewable mapping of supplied resume facts to a few manually entered application fields.
inputs: Operator supplied sample company form labels
Explicit rules for fields that must not be inferred
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator supplies a resume excerpt and a sample set of application field labels.
steps: Extract only facts explicitly present in the supplied resume.
Match each fact to a supplied field label.
Mark unmatched fields as blank and uncertain matches for review.
Show the proposed values beside their source facts.
Have the applicant correct and submit each form manually.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: On fictional examples, every filled value must match an explicitly supplied fact and uncertain or unsupported fields must remain blank.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: The applicant supplies permitted test material, checks every mapped value, decides what to disclose, and submits applications.
unverified: No browser or hiring-form integration is documented.
Resume privacy, varied form structures and reliable matching are untested.

candidates.reason: Concrete daily chore; below threshold because matching must remain manually checked, there is no implementation reference, and buyer willingness to pay is unknown.

candidates.title: Summarize multi-service order activity

demandEvidence.chore: The post proposes daily summaries of completed orders, cancellations and pending requests.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: Daily reports: Generate summaries of completed orders, cancellations, and pending requests.

ease.reason: A beginner can use test order rows; n8n Summarize documents counts and grouping, not live order intake.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: a narrow setup service might interest this group, but the discussion shows no purchase intent or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week mock can summarize supplied order rows; the reference supports aggregation, not source connections or business accuracy.

autonomy.reason: Aggregation is documented by n8n Summarize, but no trigger or report delivery is documented; a person checks results.

evidence.reason: The retained context asks about summaries of completed, cancelled and pending orders; recurrence and business demand are limited.

experimentPlan.output: Create a grouped summary of supplied order rows, counting completed, cancelled and pending requests.
inputs: Fictional order rows with a status field
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator provides a batch of sample order records for a reporting period.
steps: Check that each supplied row has an allowed status.
Group rows by the operator supplied status values.
Count orders in each group using documented aggregation behavior.
Format the counts as a draft report and flag unknown statuses.
Have an operator compare totals with the supplied rows before use.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: For a small hand-counted fictional batch, each status count and the grand total must match exactly; unknown statuses must be reported separately.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: An operator chooses permitted input fields and status definitions, checks the counts, and decides whether to share the report.
unverified: No live multi-service order source or trigger is documented.
The reference documents numeric and grouped aggregation, not semantic status interpretation or report delivery.

candidates.reason: A bounded reporting experiment is assessable, but its provisional mean is below six and source integration and buyer demand are unproved.

candidates.title: Map CRM arrays into invoice rows

demandEvidence.chore: The post asks to map a changing number of CRM array values into rows for an external invoice request.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I cannot map array data for dynamic amount of invoice rows to the HTTP POST module’s “invoice rows” section.

ease.reason: A small test can use fictional CRM rows; Make documents indexed array mapping, not invoice API execution.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: a narrow setup service might interest this group, but the discussion shows no purchase intent or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week mock can map fictional arrays; the reference covers array indexing, not invoice delivery or persistence.

autonomy.reason: The proposed loop prepares a draft; a person must verify the inputs and complete the external action.

evidence.reason: The retained spans identify dynamic invoice-row mapping from Airtable CRM data to an external REST API; posting and persistence are unverified.

experimentPlan.output: Prepare a reviewable list of invoice-row values mapped from fictional CRM arrays to operator supplied field labels.
inputs: Fictional CRM record with parallel arrays
Operator supplied invoice row field labels
Expected row count and sample output
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator supplies a fictional CRM record and the target row-field labels.
steps: Check that the supplied arrays contain the expected number of values.
Pair each item by its array index.
Flag missing or mismatched lengths instead of guessing.
Display proposed invoice rows with their original input values.
Have a person verify amounts, tax treatment and destination before any manual submission.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: For a fictional record with two values per array, output must contain two rows with index-aligned values and flag any unequal array lengths.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A person supplies authorized test data, verifies every amount and tax field, and manually decides whether to create an invoice.
unverified: Make documentation supports array item indexing but not invoice endpoint execution.
Tax correctness, external API behavior and invoice persistence are unverified.

candidates.reason: The task is concrete and a synthetic mapping test is feasible; its provisional mean is below six, while invoice delivery, persistence and tax correctness are unsupported.

candidates.title: Draft restaurant order status notifications

demandEvidence.chore: The post asks about connecting restaurant order records with customer notifications and delivery updates.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I want to understand how n8n can help connect restaurant order systems, customer notifications, and delivery updates.

ease.reason: A beginner can draft a notification from fictional order inputs; no integration capability is documented.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: a narrow setup service might interest this group, but the discussion shows no purchase intent or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week mock can draft from test orders; live order access and delivery remain unsupported.

autonomy.reason: The proposed loop prepares a draft; a person must verify the inputs and complete the external action.

evidence.reason: The post asks about connecting restaurant orders, notifications and delivery updates, but supplies no operational examples or recurrence.

experimentPlan.output: Draft a customer order-status message from one operator supplied fictional order update.
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator enters a test order update that is ready for a customer status message.
steps: Check that the order state is present and allowed.
Select the matching approved template.
Insert only the supplied state and order reference.
Flag missing or unexpected values for manual handling.
Have a staff member verify and send the draft through an approved channel.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: For each fictional status, the output must match its approved template and include no unsupplied delivery promise; unknown states must be held for review.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: Restaurant staff supply accurate state changes, approve every message and handle failed or unusual orders.
unverified: No order-system webhook, messaging integration or delivery status source is documented.
The discussion asks about a workflow but gives no live implementation evidence or repeated operational results.

candidates.reason: A bounded fictional notification draft can be scoped, but the post is exploratory, has no implementation reference, and its provisional mean is below six.
